thread:
alex (Support): Hey team — customer 'ClearWave' opened a ticket: most dashboard charts on the 'Team Usage' page are empty and the console shows 502/504s from analytics-api. They pasted one error: correlation_id=cle-502-01. Happening for ~30m.

maria (Eng): looking into logs now. any chance this aligns with the billing connector rollout earlier?

alex (Support): The user said they noticed after a billing update but not 100% certain. They can reproduce consistently on their org.

analytics-alerts: [ALERT] analytics-api upstream_errors spike — 502s increased by 420% for host analytics-prod-04 in us-west-2 (15:02 UTC).

jamal (SRE): I see increased 502s and some 504 read_timeouts from analytics sidecar to clickhouse. Stack traces show: "upstream read timeout from analytics-engine". Starting ~15:00 UTC.

maria (Eng): Reproducing locally with the same query the console issued — small SELECT with group_by over 90d. When I hit analytics-api I get 502 with body: "{"error": "upstream read timeout"}". Posting curl: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" "https://analytics.redwood/api/v1/query?panel=team_usage"```

emily (Product): Customer reports panels that used to return quickly are timing out — they care about daily active users chart. TL;DR: major UX regression for dashboards.

alex (Support): Repro steps from customer: 1) login to console, 2) open Team Usage dashboard, 3) wait ~10s, spinner persists and then blank tile with 'Error loading data' and console shows 502. They can reproduce on both org and personal account.

jamal (SRE): Quick triage: not an auth token issue — upstream returns 502 before auth service is consulted. But I do see a burst of 401s on the billing service earlier that may have changed traffic patterns.

maria (Eng): Two hypotheses: (A) a recent query planner change on analytics-engine for wide time windows causing long-running backend queries -> upstream timeout; (B) a misconfigured rate-limiter on analytics-api that began dropping connections after billing rollout. Adding trace-level logs for query routing for the next 10m.

analytics-alerts: [NOTIFICATION] Rate limiter count for /api/v1/query increased by 3.1x at 15:01 UTC.

jamal (SRE): Rolling a quick mitigation: increase upstream timeout between analytics-api and analytics-engine from 10s -> 30s for prod. Will monitor. If backend queries are slow this buys time but not a root cause fix.

maria (Eng): I pulled a sample slow query from logs: panel=team_usage, org_id=cle, sql="SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) as d, count(distinct user_id) ... GROUP BY d" — Clickhouse shows partial merges taking >20s. I'll open a perf ticket.

alex (Support): Customer confirmed that after the timeout bump their dashboard tiles started returning data intermittently (some loads still fail). They're grateful but want a permanent fix.

emily (Product): Please capture impacted customer list and bucket by frequency. Product wants to notify top affected customers and offer a workaround (shorter time windows) and status update.

maria (Eng): Action items: 1) perf ticket for clickhouse/analytics-engine query plan (assigned to eng-ml), 2) add adaptive batching / pagination in console panels to avoid huge wide-window queries, 3) verify rate-limiter config and revert any billing-induced changes to limits.

jamal (SRE): Followups: monitor 502 rate for next 2h; if still high we'll throttle background jobs and add circuit-breaker on analytics-api.

alex (Support): I'll reply to customer: escalation in progress, temporary timeout bump helped, asking them to test smaller window as workaround. Will attach correlation_id and ask for repro GIF. :thumbsup:

maria (Eng): I'll drop logs and traces here once available. For now, tagging this to eng-runtime and eng-sre on the incident board.

alex (Support): thx all — keeping this thread updated.
